div.head: ECf 11.1 B 7
div.ab: Rex dicitur a regendo, non a regno: rex eris, dum bene regis; quod nisi feceris, nomen regis non in te constabit, et nomen regis perdes, quod absit!
div.note: Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 637 (November 2026): read from the page images and checked against the scan’s own text layer, differences settled against the page.

This passage is not part of ECf or ECf retr: it is one of the additions of the London collection (Leges Anglorum s. XIII in. Londoniis collectae), which Liebermann prints in smaller type across the page, under ECf retr. 11, 1, and numbers 11, 1 A ff. The dictionary cites it as “ECf 11, 1 A …”, so it is kept with ECf here.
